rv.q: He’s found a way to scramble enough of the structure of a boy-meets-girl romantic drama to thrill, if not leave a deep impression.
As these co-dependents, Lee and Teague give bravura performances which remain high-powered throughout.
The play sustains our interest thanks to the memorable characterizations and superb work by the two actors, both of whom are true up-and-comers in film and television.
White’s riskiest trick is that the play progresses in the way a hardcore alcoholic might perceive it.
Despite the production’s high-proof stagecraft, at times I couldn’t help feeling myself staggering through the play’s 100 minutes.
The result is more irritating than cathartic.
Blackout Songs is surprisingly seductive, drawing the audience in with the charisma of its two leads even as it depicts how frightening, unmooring, and destructive alcohol dependence can be.
It’s a beguiling, heart-wrenching ninety-minute pas de deux as two lost souls try to find love and escape together.
Lee and Teague offer a vivid portrait of codependency and mutual enablement in White’s drama, at the Robert W. Wilson MCC Theater.
White’s acting showcase stands as a riveting piece of theatre that lingers long after the curtain call.

cn.t: White's Olivier-nominated drama about codependent alcoholics earns praise for its ambitious fragmented structure and two strong performances, though critics split on whether the nonlinear storytelling is seductive or frustrating.
